# KB1 supplier instantiation of the certified z4 typed echo: priced whole construction, `a < D/E`, one hosting obstruction

Agent: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent human review claimed). No model is named. Base main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`; priority revision 4; selected record unchanged; **no new kappa and no supplier admission**.

Package: `research/z4-typed-echo-supplier-instance/`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18947139

## What this is

Every mechanism package in this repo ends with "no supplier instance exists, so no kappa change follows". This PR closes that gap for one certified mechanism as far as the repository's contracts allow: the **z4 order-four typed echo** (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1391 five-child contract, [PR 1410](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1410) persistent pair, both pinned through `research/z4-persistent-pair-seed57/inputs`). The deliverable is a supplier instantiation with (1) the smallest falsifying instance first, (2) the priced whole-construction budget (dispatch, instruction fetch, coefficient fetch, reads, writes, address travel, descriptor storage, data storage), (3) the hosted ledgers' exact moments and the `a < D/E` diagnostics, (4) exact controls, (5) one documented obstruction in exactly one obligation, and one bounded pivot.

**Scope status: changed** (recorded in `TASK.json` with the reason). The drawn card was `connector-alphabet-change` (scope key `ff4f5113ed2256ab19ed`); this session takes the explicitly assigned kappa-blocker KB1 request instead. Two of the three named KB1 candidates carry fresh same-day claims, so the object is the unclaimed z4 typed echo: DUO connector words (https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2396, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2397, comment 18943467 at 07:26 UTC) and R439 star absorption (comment 18944326 released at 18945494; https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2407, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2421, https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2428) were excluded by the pair-collision check (`disc-comments` with nested replies on discussions 1166 and 1317, 2026-10-15 10:35-10:40 UTC; overlap refreshed again at 11:27 UTC). The instantiation is registered under the `centre-path-sharing` card because that is the lever it prices.

## Results

**Mechanism rebuilt and falsified at the smallest instance.** Boundary schedule re-derived by an independent dynamic program and checked against the pinned brute force: `g(1)=60, g(2)=88, g(3)=116, g(5)=140, g(10)=248`. Smallest falsifying instance first: the k=2 typed pair (two one-child echoes fused into one two-child echo), all 16 phase paths, all 56 basis columns (every dirty state exactly, by linearity), joint equals sequential composition, literal inverse exact; three schedule mutants (wrong first output phase, omitted terminal gap, forward-for-inverse) rejected. The pinned invoices reproduce exactly.

| schedule | ADD | NEG | total | comparison |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| five-child echo | 920 | 88 | 1,008 | eager 1,328 ([PR 1391](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1391)) |
| ten-child joint echo | 1,720 | 184 | 1,904 | two separate 2,016 ([PR 1410](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1410)) |
| two-child joint echo | 440 | 56 | 496 | two separate 608 (this PR) |

Prefix row-L1 peaks: 4 at k=1, 10 at k=2, 20 at k=5, 30 for two separate five-child calls, 42 for the joint ten-child call, reproducing [PR 1410](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1410)'s 30/42.

**Priced whole-construction budget** (declared model: rows of width 73 on a row-indexed tape; dispatch, instruction fetch and coefficient fetch per record; ADD reads 2 writes 1, NEG reads 1 writes 1; address travel `2*max(source,target)` per record, the `research/mutable-source-persistent-connector` convention; 16-bit descriptor per record plus 128-bit call record; 56*width data cells):

| quantity | two separate calls (k=2) | joint k=2 | saving per pair |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| primitives | 608 | 496 | 112 |
| dispatches | 608 | 496 | 112 |
| instruction fetches | 608 | 496 | 112 |
| coefficient fetches | 608 | 496 | 112 |
| reads | 1,168 | 936 | 232 |
| writes | 608 | 496 | 112 |
| address travel (row steps) | 53,024 | 36,944 | 16,080 |
| descriptor bits | 9,984 | 8,064 | 1,920 |
| data storage cells | 4,088 | 4,088 | 0 |

The k=5+5 versus k=10 pair has identical savings. The saving is scalar: no moment-ledger quantity moves.

**Hosted ledgers and the `a < D/E` diagnostic** (named host: the binding selected complex ledger, m=73, W=14,336, N=144, published histogram; the typed echo realizes the shared-centre ledger of `research/centre-sharing-overhead-budget`, n_8 1,152 to 576, coverage `72W + 32N`; exact rational atanh/Taylor enclosures, independently implemented):

| ledger | rank mass | D | a < D/E | exact moment root a* |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| selected baseline | 1,041,408 | 5,120 | 0.0016805907097543218 | [0.001675462676, 0.001675462677] |
| shared k=2 typed echo | 1,036,800 | 9,728 | 0.003203836729943888 | [0.003185242415, 0.003185242416] |

The baseline `D/E` matches the published 0.001680590709754321699421 to 2.4e-25 (its printing precision) and the baseline root is the recorded complex endpoint 0.0016754626768081035 (residual in the published minus-1.30e-24 band; the next 1e-24 grid point is rejected). At the recorded bit endpoint 0.0017334270395898442 the shared ledger gives `f(a) - 1 = -4.25e-3`, matching `research/centre-sharing-overhead-budget`'s table entry. With sharing the complex side stops binding and the whole bound becomes bit-limited at `kappa = 0.001730427469823602` (+3.4536%), that package's published figure, here reached by a concrete mechanism instead of a relaxation. A control enforces that `D/E` is only a screen: the exact moment at `D/E` exceeds 1 strictly.

**Delta-H fits the sharpest budget.** The typed echo eliminates one wrapper per pair: 8 rank-8 children, 64 rank units per pair, 32 per call. Its added work is scalar, so its recursive overhead is 0 rank units; the sharp full-gain budget of `research/centre-sharing-overhead-budget` allows 30.5 to 30.8 units per call (any gain below 31.9 to 32.0).

## The one obstruction: hosting (window lifetime and totals delivery)

The fused pair defers the first call wrapper's `W -= X` (the ERASE analogue) past the second call's block. The k=2 witness is exact: all 24 work rows are dirty at the second block's entry, where the separate schedule has already restored. The pinned host contract (`research/split-centres-global/proofs/PR386-BIT-GEOMETRY.txt`) keeps COPY/ERASE windows sequential and immutable and delivers totals per call through each call's private temporary. The typed carry needs one window spanning the pair, per-pair totals delivery, and uninterrupted ownership. Under the unchanged contract the pair pays both wrappers, `n_8` stays 1,152, the moment is exactly the selected one, and 112 saved primitives change nothing. A contract change would also need a child exposing the order-four intertwiner `R P = Q R` and a common sink for the pair's totals (the first blocker of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1748). The source-bound side is already recorded: `research/selected-centre-adjacent-pair-seed01fcb1` found no adjacent pair of the pinned 144-call schedule sharing one physical owner among its eight centre source rows; its escapes (aliases, paid owner transport, changed schedule) are this same obligation.

**Bounded pivot (one): single-call realization.** Make the pair one supplier call, so one window stays sequential and immutable. The per-call totals contract then makes the fused call copy both calls' totals: 16 rank-8 children per pair, 128 rank units, exactly the two-wrapper baseline. The ledger returns to the selected histogram and the moment is identical (checked exactly); sharing one totals set is the same contract change. The route stops here.

```sh
python3 -B research/z4-typed-echo-supplier-instance/verify.py
```

```text
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/z4-typed-echo-supplier-instance outcome=completed
```

`python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` passes (65 tests, 3 skipped). 51 controls cover the mechanism reproductions, smallest-instance map and inverse identities, three schedule mutants, wrapper counts and the deferred-restoration witness, dispatch charges, row-L1 reproduction, both coverage identities, the published `D/E` and residual bands, the `D/E`-is-not-acceptance control, the Delta-H budget fit, the pivot's identical moment, and three mutated-ledger rejections.

Not checked: native or hosted emission, the complex host's precision bucket law (the carry raises prefix row-L1 from 30 to 42; priced in the table above but not admitted), all-size/compiler, common-label/mutable-source realization, tape, analytic transfer, bit H1-H5. Not a multiplication theorem; no supplier admitted.
